The nodes are colored so that no two neighbors share a color, and each color class adopts its neighbors' most common label at once; with no randomness, the labels settle on the two groups, drawn in the accent color and teal. The card lists community 0 as A, B, C, D and community 1 as E, F, G, H." width="100%"} Label propagation lets every node adopt the label most common among its neighbors until labels settle into communities. Updating all nodes at once (synchronously) can make labels flip back and forth forever, for example across the two sides of a bipartite graph, while updating them one at a time in random order (as `cmty_label_propagation()` does) gives a different answer on each run. The semi-synchronous method (Cordasco and Gargano, 2010) takes the middle way: it colors the graph so that no two neighbors share a color and updates one color class at a time. Neighbors never update together, so labels cannot oscillate, and with ties broken by a fixed rule the result is deterministic. There is no seed: the same graph always gives the same communities. Edge direction and edge weights are ignored, and parallel edges count once. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Node attribute to store the communities in (default `"cmty_semisync_label_propagation"`). [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, return the node-to-community dictionary instead of storing it. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, int], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : With `return_dict=True`, a dictionary mapping node IDs to community labels (numbered in order of the lowest node ID in each); otherwise `self`. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~cmty_label_propagation`) : Asynchronous label propagation, in random order. [](`~cmty_fast_label_propagation`) : Label propagation that revisits only changed nodes. ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The coloring is greedy, taking the nodes in order of decreasing degree with ties by ID and giving each the smallest color its neighbors have not used (the order NetworkX's `greedy_color()` uses by default). Every node starts with its own label, numbered in ID order. Then, color by color, each node takes the label most frequent among its neighbors; on a tie it keeps its label if that is one of the most frequent, and otherwise takes the highest (the Prec-Max rule). The rounds stop once every node with neighbors holds one of its most frequent neighbor labels, which the method is proven to reach. Each round takes $O(V + E)$. Matches NetworkX's `label_propagation_communities`, which raises an error for directed graphs where EdgeCase ignores direction. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Zachary's karate club splits into three groups, and the same three on every run: ::: {#83970396 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec club = ec.karate_club() communities = club.cmty_semisync_label_propagation(return_dict=True) sorted(list(communities.values()).count(c) for c in set(communities.values())) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [3, 15, 16] ``` ::: :::
